newsitem.title: UK: Ford aims for 1,000 job cuts in Britain.
newsitem.headline: Ford aims for 1,000 job cuts in Britain.

text.p: Ford Motor Co. aims to cut 1,000 jobs at plants in Britain through voluntary reductions and early retirement, a company spokesman told Reuters Wednesday.
He said the move was part of "the ongoing drive to ensure all our plants in the UK are fully competitive on a global basis."
The spokesman said all the U.S. company's larger plants in Britain had targets for job cuts but any job losses would be voluntary and the company had the full cooperation of unions.

Ford has major plants at Dagenham in east London and Halewood on Merseyside, northwest England, as well as smaller facilities at Southampton, southern England, and Bridgend and Swansea in Wales. It employs around 30,000 workers in Britain.
Last week, there were unconfirmed newspaper reports that Ford intended to cut 1,000 jobs at Halewood as a result of a plan to replace in-house production of components with outside suppliers.
